memory_candidates.content: In LLM-executed prose skill files (skill-*/SKILL.md), variable interpolations inside dispatch prompts are never checked by any compiler or shell, so a prompt can reference a variable that no stage in that code path ever assigns and the failure is completely silent -- the interpolation renders empty and the dispatch still 'succeeds'. This bug class was found in skill-orchestrate's multi-task path, where three dispatch loops interpolated $description but only task_type/project_name were ever captured. It is worth grepping for the assignment of every variable interpolated in a dispatch prompt whenever adding a consumer that hard-requires one (e.g. memory-retrieve.sh exits 1 on empty description). The general mitigation is a loud non-blocking emptiness warning at the shared consumption point, which makes the whole class self-diagnosing on regression rather than requiring per-variable audits.
